From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Buying committee recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk the committee through the demo. Appreciate the candid questions — below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Attendees (as I had them):
- Alex Green — CFO / economic buyer
- Maya Liu — Head of Data & AI / technical sponsor
- (Redwood) Marissa Cole — AE
- (Redwood) Lukas Meyer — Solutions Engineer

Key takeaways from the demo:
- Decision criteria: predictable latency under 200ms for interactive flows, per-token cost target <$0.0008, and SOC2/audit evidence for procurement.
- Primary workloads: customer support summarization (low latency), and nightly batch embeddings for search (throughput).
- Risk areas called out: data residency for EU customers (Maya) and contractual SLAs (Alex).

Immediate asks we captured:
1) Security evidence (SOC2 summary, config options for VPC/private deployment) — Lukas to share short packet.
2) Procurement/legal items: proposed contract terms, SLA, and pricing model (usage vs committed) — Marissa to propose a draft MAP + quote.
3) Pilot: 4-week POC to validate latency/throughput on representative sample — Lukas to propose test plan.

Attachments: MAP-FinTechCo-20270110.xlsx (draft mutual action plan), redwood-security-summary.pdf (top-level packet).

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- This week (by Wed 1/13): Lukas shares SOC2 & POC test plan; Marissa shares draft MAP and ballpark pricing.
- Next Tue (1/19): Procurement/legal call to review contract and data residency obligations.
- Week of 2/1: Kickoff 4-week pilot (contingent on procurement).

Please confirm if I've missed anyone on attendees or if the timeline works. If procurement/legal need a separate intro thread, drop the contact and I'll add them.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183

--
Redwood Inference | Production-grade LLM inference: hosted, dedicated, private
From: Alex Green <alex.green@fintechco.com>

Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Buying committee recap & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the tidy recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Economic buyer/contract: I'll be the signatory for commercial terms, but procurement will handle PO/standard terms review. Please include our procurement team (procurement@fintechco.com) on the contract thread.
- Security/compliance: we need a SOC2 Type II report (or summary + auditor) and a clear data residency statement for EU customer data. Is there a hosted EU region or do you offer Private (VPC) deployments for regulated workloads?
- Pricing: we prefer a committed throughput contract with a burst allowance if possible. Can you provide a committed vs on-demand pricing example for our expected volumes (est. 5M tokens/month interactive + 100k embeddings/month)?

Also, for legal procurement scheduling, can you book a 30-minute slot next Tue (1/19) between 10a–12p PT? I'll loop in our legal counsel if the draft MAP/terms look reasonable.

Thanks —
Alex
Alex Green
CFO, FinTechCo
alex.green@fintechco.com | (415) 212-9982

Alex / Maya —

Appreciate the follow-ups. Short answers and attachments below.

1) SOC2 / security evidence: attached redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (executive summary + auditor contact) and redwood-security-summary.pdf (config options). We can provide SOC2 Type II full report under an NDA; the summary includes our control scopes relevant to data handling/segregation.

2) Data residency: We offer hosted regions in US and EU (Frankfurt). For regulated EU customer data we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or a Dedicated cluster pinned to the EU region. Private deployments support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

3) Pricing example (ballpark based on stated volumes):
- Committed monthly commit (5M tokens interactive + 100k embeddings): ~$X,XXX/month with 15% discount over on-demand; includes predictable throughput and reserved capacity.
- On-demand: metered per-token with higher unit costs and no guaranteed throughput.

4) Pilot plan: 4-week POC to validate latency and KV cache behavior. Proposed test plan attached in MAP (sheet: POC plan). Key acceptance criteria: median p95 latency <200ms for interactive subset, embedding recall within 2% of baseline.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-security-summary.pdf. I'll also upload the full SOC2 under NDA if you'd like.

Happy to join the procurement/legal call. Marissa — can you schedule for Tue 1/19 10:30a PT?

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
